dedupe_keys.name: infrastructure investment in portugal volume i database and stylised facts 1978 to 2011 ffms

description: Investimento em Infraestruturas em Portugal, volume I, is a 584-page study by the economists Alfredo and Rui Marvão Pereira, published by the Francisco Manuel dos Santos Foundation, that builds and describes a database of infrastructure investment in Portugal from 1978 to 2011. The database is given at current and constant prices, nationally and by region, and later chapters document investment by infrastructure type with its institutional setting and sources, including the national road network, municipal roads, health, education, water supply and treatment, electricity and gas, petroleum refining and telecommunications. The final part draws stylised facts nationally and for each region, such as the North. The report is a free PDF online; no licence is stated in the pages read. Caveats: the series end in 2011, and the data is presented in the report's tables, not as a separate machine-readable file in what was read. Coverage is Portugal, with regional breakdowns. It supports economic and capacity planning analysis of long-run infrastructure investment across transport, energy, water, telecom and social sectors, such as comparing investment cycles with asset condition; related records are the Te Waihanga National Infrastructure Pipeline and OpenCUP of Italy.
